contexts.text: That charity was extinguished with those who separated faith, and set it before charity, is described by Cain, that he killed his brother Abel. AC 366. AC 369.

Everyone who finds me will kill me () = that all evil and falsity will destroy him. (For) when a man deprives himself of charity... whatever he thinks is false, and whatever he wills is evil. These are the things which kill man, or which cause him to have no life.
That those who are in evil and falsity are in continual terror of being killed. Illustrated.
Those who on earth have been violent and unmerciful... seem to themselves to kill and torment (their) companions.

For in hatred there is the very killing of a man, as is manifestly evident from the fact that he who is in hatred wishes for nothing more than that he may kill the other; and, unless external bonds hindered, he would kill him. Therefore the killing of a brother, and the shedding of his blood, = hatred...
They will kill me [Abram] () = that they will not care for celestial things.
The commandment Thou shalt not kill is altogether of charity...
Wilt Thou kill also a just nation? () = whether good and truth should be extinguished.
They will kill me [Abraham] on account of the word of my wife () = that thus the celestial things of faith would also perish... To kill = to perish.
(By) Thou shalt not kill, the Angels perceived that they should not hold anyone in hatred, and that they should not extinguish anything of good and truth with anyone...
To kill the root with hunger, and to kill the remains () = to take away the goods and truths which have been stored up interiorly by the Lord.
Without any perception of conscience he would steal, kill, and commit adultery.
For he who hates anyone, kills him every moment.
Lest the men of the place kill me for the sake of Rebekah () = because thus Divine good would not be received.
To commit murder = to bear hatred; for he who hates another commits murder every moment...
Then shall they... kill you () = that good and truth would perish... by denial. That to kill, when predicated of good and truth, = not to be received, thus to deny. References.
I will kill my brother Jacob () = to deprive truth of life from itself. Explained. AC 3610.
They kill in the way to Shechem () = that they extinguish truths even to interior ones, thus all external ones.
This is the secret reason why Hamor and Shechem with their families were killed.
Because in their anger they killed a man, and in their own good pleasure they hamstrung an ox () = that in purposed evil they extinguished the truth and good of the Church.
Now come and let us kill him () = the extinction of the essential of doctrine concerning the Lord's Divine Human. To kill = to extinguish.
The raiment of the slain () = truth profaned.
What gain is it that we kill our brother, and cover his blood? () = that from this there would be nothing profitable... if this should be completely extinguished.
Avarice would kill for a mere trifle.
They believe... that all the rest in the world are... so vile that they may be killed at pleasure.
The slain () = those who by principles of falsity have extinguished the truths of faith in themselves, in a less degree than the thrust through.

In that Hell are those who... have wanted to destroy the human race, namely, to kill and despoil without respect or distinction... Such ferocity prevails in many soldiers... who, not in battle, but after it, rage with ferocity against the conquered and unarmed, and with fury kill and despoil.
That he who does this is damned, is signified by the command that he shall be put to death ().
Because in their anger they killed a man = that they completely averted themselves, and in their aversion extinguished faith... To kill = to extinguish.
If it be a son then ye shall kill him () = that if it were truth they should destroy it in any way they could... To kill = to destroy; for it is said of truth.

Sayest thou to kill me? () = dost thou want to destroy my faith?... He who destroys faith with anyone destroys the Church with him; and this is also to kill him; for he who takes away faith takes away spiritual life...
That to kill = to take away spiritual life, is evident from many places in the Word. Illustrated.
The day of killing () = the time of the vastation of the Church, when there is no longer any faith, because no charity.
The sheep of killing () = those whose faith the possessors destroy. AC 8902:7.
To kill () = to destroy spiritual life; that is, faith and charity.
The killed () = those who are in Hell, thus who are in evils and falsities.
The killed () = those who are deprived of spiritual life. Thou hast killed thy people = that he has destroyed the truths and goods of faith.
The thief cometh not except... to kill... (). To kill = to destroy the life of faith.

The brother shall betray the brother to death, and the father the children; and the children shall rise up against their parents, and shall kill them () ... Brother, children, and parents = the goods and truths of the Church; and to kill = to destroy them.
As by one who had been killed was signified one who has been deprived of spiritual life... it was a statute... that if anyone touched... one who had been killed, he should be unclean seven days ().
As thou killedst the Egyptian () = as thou destroyedst falsity.
Pharaoh... sought to kill Moses () = that the false Scientific... wanted to destroy the truth which is of the Law from the Divine.
To kill the soul () = ... to die spiritually or be damned.
I will kill thy son, thy first-born () = the extinction of the faith which is devoid of charity, and the consequent devastation of truth with them.
Jehovah... sought to kill (Moses) () = that a representative Church could not be instituted with that nation. To seek to kill = not to receive.
In the Heavens they do not know what it is to commit murder; for they live to eternity; but instead of to commit murder they understand to bear hatred, and to injure the spiritual life of anyone.
To put a sword in their hand to kill us () = that hence they feel such ardour to destroy by falsities the truths of the Church... To kill = to destroy the things which are of faith and charity.

To kill all this congregation with hunger () = that from defect of delight and of good they would expire. To kill = to deprive of life; here, of the life which is from delight and from good; for in these the life of man consists. Explained.

Thou shalt not commit murder () = not to take away spiritual life from anyone; also not to extinguish faith and charity; and also not to bear hatred to the neighbour. (For) to kill = to deprive of spiritual life... because, in the internal sense, it treats of the spiritual... life of man; and as spiritual life or the life of Heaven with man is the life of faith and charity, therefore by not to commit murder is also signified not to extinguish faith and charity with anyone. The reason not to commit murder = not to bear hatred to the neighbour, is that he who bears hatred continually wants to kill, and also would kill in act unless prevented by the fear of the penalty, etc.; for hatred... breathes nothing but the murder of him whom it hates, in the world the murder of his body, in the other life the murder of his soul. This is meant by the Lord's words in .

That to commit murder or kill = to take away spiritual life from anyone, and consequently to extinguish faith and charity, is evident from almost all the passages in the Word where killing is mentioned, or the expression to kill is used. Illustrated.
Killers () = those who destroy goods and truths.

They shall kill you (). The hour cometh, that everyone who killeth you will think that he offers holy worship to God (). Here also by to kill is signified to deprive of spiritual life; that is, of faith and charity.
To kill () = to extinguish.
The slain () = those who have perished as to spiritual life.
As by one slain or thrust through is signified the extinction of good and truth...
(Thus) the commandment about not committing murder involves not only that a man is not to be killed as to the body, but also that he is not to be killed as to the soul...
In order that these things might be signified by those who kill their companions by mistake ().
To kill him with deceit () = malice thence to deprive the neighbour of eternal life. To kill = to take away faith and charity from the neighbour, and thus to deprive him of spiritual life.
And (the ox) hath slain a man or a woman () = if it has destroyed the truth and good of faith.
Belshazzar's being slain in that night () = the privation of the life of truth and good, thus damnation.

I will kill you with the sword () = that by falsities they deprive themselves of good and truth. To kill, when said of those who defraud those who are in good and truth... = to deprive them of such things. That to kill = to deprive of spiritual life. References.
The innocent and the just kill thou not () = aversion to the destroying of interior and exterior good... To kill = to destroy. AC 9264.
Such are permitted to destroy, and to kill... but not those who are in externals and at the same time in internals, because these act from good, and good is from the Lord.
The slayer () = one who deprives of spiritual life, or of life from good and truth. References.
To be cut off, and to be killed, = to be separated from those who are in good and the derivative truths, and to perish as to spiritual life.

For evil He hath brought them forth to kill them in the mountains () = that those who are in good would perish. To bring forth to kill = to destroy; but, when said of Jehovah, who never destroys anyone, it = to perish by their own evil.

Kill ye a man his brother, and a man his companion, and a man his neighbour () = a closing up as to the influx of good and truth, and of things in affinity with them, lest there should be any reception and communication. To kill = to take away spiritual life, thus the good of love and the truth of faith; here, therefore, to close up lest there should be any reception and communication of them...
Although he does not commit murder, still he bears hatred to everyone who opposes him... and unless external bonds... restrained, he would commit murder.
Therefore it is the delight of their life to want to destroy and kill...

By to commit murder, man understands to bear hatred, and to desire revenge even to murder... A spiritual Angel understands by it to act as a devil, and to murder a man's soul. A celestial Angel understands by it to bear hatred to the Lord, and to the things which are of the Lord. AE 1083:6.
Antipas... was slain among you where Satan dwelleth () = when all Truth has been extinguished by the falsities in the Church. ( = when all are hated who acknowledge the Lord's Divine Human. AE 137.)

I will kill her sons with death () = that all truths from the Word with them will be turned into falsities... To kill sons = to turn truths into falsities, for so they perish. ( = that thus falsities are extinguished. AE 166.)
A lamb standing as if slain () = the Lord as to the Human not acknowledged in the Church to be Divine. ( = as yet acknowledged by few. AE 315.)
That they should kill one another () = intestine hatreds, infestations by the Hells, and internal unrest. ( = the falsification or extinction of truths. AE 366).

The souls of them that were slain for the Word of God, and for the testimony which they held () = those who had been hated, reproached, and rejected by the evil, on account of a life according to the truths of the Word, and the acknowledgement of the Lord's Divine Human. AE 392. AR 329.

That by the slain are meant those who are rejected, treated with abuse, and held in hatred by the evil in the World of Spirits, and who can be seduced; and also those who long to know truths, but cannot on account of the falsities in the Church. Illustrated.

Not to be able to kill them () = not to be able to take away from those who are not in the faith of charity the faculty of understanding and willing truth and good; for when this faculty is taken away the man is spiritually killed. AE 547.
To kill a third part of men () = to take away from the men of the Church spiritual light and life. ( = to deprive themselves of all the understanding of truth, and thence of spiritual life. AE 572.)

By these three was a third part of men killed () = that it is from these things that the men of the Church perish. ( = that all the understanding of truth and the derivative spiritual life was extinguished by them. AE 579.)
To be killed = to be spiritually killed, which is to perish as to the soul.
If anyone will hurt them, thus must he be killed () = that he who condemns them shall in like manner be condemned. ( = that they perish according to the endeavour to inflict evil. AE 643.)

The beast... shall kill them () = that those who are in the internals of the doctrine of faith alone... will themselves reject them, and, so far as they have influence, will cause others to reject them. ( = the destruction thereby of all the good and truth of the Church. AE 651.)

There were killed in the earthquake names of men seven thousand () = that in that state all those who professed faith alone... perished. ( = that in that change of state all truths of good perished with them, and thereby all things of Heaven and the Church. AE 676.)
Slain from the foundation of the world () = the Lord's Divine Human not acknowledged from the establishment of the Church. AE 807.
If anyone shall kill with the sword, he must be killed with the sword () = that he who by falsities destroys the soul of another, shall be destroyed and shall perish by falsities. AE 812.
As many as would not worship the image of the beast should be killed () = damnation upon those who do not acknowledge the doctrine of their faith. AE 833.
To be killed = to be spiritually killed, which is to be damned; and (therefore) to be killed = to be declared a heretic, and to be excluded from the communion of the Church...
By them that are slain () are signified those who have been spiritually slain; and those are said to be spiritually slain who perish by falsities. Reference. AE 1194.

The rest were slain with the sword of Him who sat upon the horse... () = that all from the various heresies among the Reformed who have not lived according to the Lord's precepts... having been judged from the Word, perish.
To be killed, pierced, or dead... (means) that they have been rejected by those who are in evils and falsities.

Thou shalt not commit murder, in the natural sense, means not to kill a man, not to inflict on him any wound of which he may die, and also not to mutilate his body; and it means, moreover, not to bring any deadly evil upon his name and reputation, because with many reputation and life go hand in hand. In a wider natural sense, by murders are meant enmities, hatreds, and revenges, which breathe murder. (Continued. See Murder, and at TCR 310.)
Those who are destroyed by falsities, are meant by the slain. Illustrated.
In the celestial sense, to commit murder means to be rashly angry with the Lord, to hate Him, and to want to blot out His name... This is meant by the lamb standing as it had been slain.

Devils and Satans bear continually in mind to kill the Lord; and, as they cannot do this, they are in the endeavour to kill those who are devoted to the Lord; and as they cannot do this like men in the world, they make every effort to destroy their souls; that is, to destroy faith and charity with them.
On those who in life deceitfully kill men.

A tumult under the sole of the left foot (indicated) those who have been obsessed by the cupidity of fighting and killing men... In the other life they seem to themselves to kill and lacerate each other... They are miserably treated there...
That the endeavour of the interior evil Spirits is to kill.
Among the magical arts is this, - that they inspire others with anger... in order that they may kill themselves...
(The Moravians) killed a man who had divulged their secrets. SE 4806. SE 4807. SE 4808.
To kill the souls that ought not to die () = to deprive them of life from truths.
The Lord is said to be spiritually killed when the truth which is from Him is denied, and the good rejected...
That to be killed = to be spiritually killed. Illustrated.

For Thou hast been slain, and hast redeemed us to God in Thy blood () = the separation of all from the Divine, and conjunction with the Divine by the acknowledgement of Him and by the reception of Divine truth from Him. To be slain, when said of the Lord, = the separation of all from the Divine; for to be slain, in the Word, = to be spiritually slain; that is, to perish from evils and falsities; and as the Lord is not with them therefore by slain, when said of the Lord, is signified not acknowledged, and also denied; and, when the Lord is denied, He is as it were slain with them, and thereby they are separated from the Divine...
The slain = those who have perished by falsities and evils. AE 329:28.
The lamb that was slain () = the Lord's Divine Human not acknowledged, and by many denied.
To kill = to extinguish. AE 589:end.
Their damnation is signified by their being slain.
The slain = those with whom there is not any spiritual life.
To smite, and to kill, = to be damned...
To kill = to destroy.
The rest of the men who were not killed () = all those who did not perish. To be killed = to be spiritually killed, which is to perish in eternal death.
To kill, spiritually, = to extinguish the spiritual life, which is done through the falsities of evil.
To kill the prophets = to destroy the Divine.
(Thus) to kill relates to the truth of doctrine of the Church...; to crucify, to the good of doctrine.
Murderers () = those who destroy the spiritual life of man by falsities and evils.
Slay to destruction () = to completely destroy.
Thou shalt not commit murder contains also not to bear hatred to the neighbour, and not to love revenge; for hatreds and revenges breathe murder.

The proximate sense of this precept, Thou shalt not commit murder, which is the spiritual moral sense, is, Thou shalt not hate thy brother or neighbour, and thus not treat him with contumely and ignominy; for thus thou injurest and killest his reputation and honour, from which is his life among his brethren, which life is called civil; whence he will afterwards live in society as it were dead... This, when done from enmity, from hatred, or from revenge, is murder... and he who does it is as guilty before the Angels as if he had killed his brother as to the life of the body; for enmity, hatred, and revenge breathe murder and will it... These three are an endeavour to murder; and all endeavour is as it were an act...

But the more remote sense of... Thou shalt not commit murder, which is called the celestial spiritual sense, is, Thou shalt not take away from a man the faith and love of God, and thereby his spiritual life. This is murder itself. (Continued. See Murder.)

The delight of doing evil from hatred, which breathes forth from Hell, is the delight of killing; but as they cannot kill the body, they want to kill the spirit... From these things it is evident that the precept, Thou shalt not commit murder involves also, Thou shalt not bear hatred to thy neighbour; likewise, Thou shalt not bear hatred to the good of the Church and its truth; for if thou hatest good and truth, then thou hatest the neighbour, and to hate is to want to kill. Hence it is that the devil... is called a murderer from the beginning.

5. 4. Take the fifth precept, Thou shalt not commit murder. The Spiritual in it is, Thou shalt not deny God, thus the Lord; for to deny Him is to kill and crucify Him in yourself: and also, Thou shalt not destroy the spiritual life which a man has; for thus thou killest his soul. The Moral is, Thou shalt not bear hatred to the neighbour, and wish for revenge against him... And the Civil is, Thou shalt not kill his body.
